newsitem.title: SWEDEN: P&U says Fragmin gets Swedish, British nod as heart treatment.
newsitem.headline: P&U says Fragmin gets Swedish, British nod as heart treatment.

text.p: Swedish-U.S. pharmaceutical group Pharmacia & Upjohn said Monday it had received approval in Sweden and Britain to sell Fragmin for the treatment of unstable coronary arteries.
About 40 percent of patients admitted to hospitals' heart units have unstable coronary arteries, which often leads to heart attacks and death, the company said.
"Fragmin can reduce the number of heart attacks and deaths by up to 60 percent if added to standard treatments," the company said.
About 40,000 patients in Sweden and about 300,000 patients in Britain are affected each year, Pharmacia & Upjohn said.
An advantage of Fragmin is that the patient does not have to be confined to continuous intravenous treatment, the company said.
